title: Recording: Everybody’s In A Hurry But Me by Ringo Starr | 1982
content:
Startling Studios, Ascot
Producers: Joe Walsh, Russ Ballard
Engineer: Jim Nipar

Ringo Starr recorded ‘Everybody’s In A Hurry But Me’ for his ninth studio album, Old Wave, on 14 March 1982.

The song was the result of a studio jam featuring Eric Clapton and Joe Walsh on guitars, The Who’s John Entwistle on bass, and Ray Cooper on percussion. The jam took place on this day at Startling Studios, in Starr’s Tittenhurst Park home. Also present was Pattie Boyd, then married to Clapton.

Several rehearsal takes were recorded and the arrangement tweaked before the final version was completed. Walsh later overdubbed extra guitar parts, and Starr’s lead vocals were added at Santa Barbara Sound Recording on 6 August 1982.

Page last updated: 3 June 2026
